titulo_es: Cleft sentences (It was… that…, What I need is…)
descripcion_es: Highlighting one part of the sentence with It is/was… that/who… and with What… is/was…
resumen: Cleft sentences split a sentence into two parts to put the focus on one particular element, like Spanish “fue Juan quien…” or “lo que necesito es…”. English cannot move the stress as freely as Spanish, so it uses them a lot.

explicacion.texto: It-cleft: It + be + highlighted element + that/who + rest. It is used to highlight the subject, the object or an adverbial, often to contrast: It was Maria who/that found the keys (not anyone else).

Wh-cleft (pseudo-cleft): What + subject + verb + be + highlighted element. It puts the focus at the end: What I need is a holiday. To highlight an action you use do: What she did was (to) call the police.

filas: It was Tom who broke the window.
It was in Rome that I met her.
It was only yesterday that we noticed it.
What I want is some peace.
What happened was (that) he lost his job.

items: Other variants: All I want is… (the only thing I want is…), The thing that annoys me is…, The reason why… is that…, The place where… is…
In the it-cleft the verb be agrees with it (singular) even if the focus is plural: It is the students who complain.
In the part with that/who, the verb agrees with the highlighted element: It is I who am wrong (formal) / It's me who's wrong (informal).
With a person as subject, who is preferred; for everything else, that.

ejemplos.frase: It was my grandfather who taught me to fish.
ejemplos.traduccion: Fue mi abuelo quien me enseñó a pescar.

ejemplos.frase: It's not the money that worries me, it's the time.
ejemplos.traduccion: No es el dinero lo que me preocupa, es el tiempo.

ejemplos.frase: What surprised everyone was how calm she remained.
ejemplos.traduccion: Lo que sorprendió a todos fue lo tranquila que se mantuvo.

ejemplos.frase: All we need is a bit of luck.
ejemplos.traduccion: Lo único que necesitamos es un poco de suerte.

ejemplos.frase: What the committee did was postpone the decision.
ejemplos.traduccion: Lo que hizo el comité fue aplazar la decisión.

ejemplos.frase: It was not until 1975 that the law was changed.
ejemplos.traduccion: No fue hasta 1975 cuando se cambió la ley.

errores_hispanohablantes.bien: It was Peter who called you.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: In English the subject it is compulsory; it cannot be left out as in Spanish “Fue Peter quien…”.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: It was in 2010 when I moved to London.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: It was in 2010 that I moved to London.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: After a time adverbial with a preposition, the it-cleft uses that; when sounds informal or wrong (Spanish does say “cuando”).

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: The thing what I hate is waiting.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: What already means “the thing that”; with the thing you use that: The thing that I hate is waiting.

ejercicios.frase: It was the manager ___ approved the budget.
respuestas: who
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the card's it-cleft: It + be + highlighted element + that/who + rest. The clue is that the highlighted element, “the manager”, is a person and is also the subject of “approved”; with people as subjects “who” is preferred, although “that” would also be correct. That is why “It was the manager who approved the budget”. The second part does not repeat the subject.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: The highlighted element is a person and the subject: who (or that).
ejercicios.traduccion: Fue el director quien aprobó el presupuesto.

por_opcion.who: Correct: relative pronoun for a person who is the subject of “approved”.
por_opcion.what: Incorrect: “what” means “the thing that” and cannot introduce the second part of an it-cleft.
por_opcion.which he: Incorrect: “which” is used for things, and “he” also repeats the subject, which English does not allow in a relative clause.
por_opcion.whom: Incorrect: “whom” is an object form, and here the highlighted element is the subject of “approved”.

glosario.definicion_l: a sum of money allocated for a particular purpose · a summary of intended expenditures along with proposals for how to meet them

ejercicios.frase: ___ I really need is a good night's sleep.
respuestas: What
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the card's wh-cleft: What + subject + verb + be + highlighted element. The clue is the structure “___ I really need is…”: the first part corresponds to Spanish “lo que necesito”, and in English “lo que” is “what”. That is why “What I really need is a good night's sleep”. The focus stays at the end, on what is needed.
ejercicios.traduccion: Lo que de verdad necesito es una buena noche de sueño.

por_opcion.That: Incorrect: “that” does not mean “the thing that”; the card includes “The thing that…”, but without “the thing” it does not work.
por_opcion.Which: Incorrect: “which” needs an antecedent; it cannot open the sentence with the meaning “the thing that”.
por_opcion.What: Correct: “what” introduces the wh-cleft with the meaning “the thing that”.
por_opcion.It: Incorrect: “It I really need is…” is not grammatical; the it-cleft would be “It is a good night's sleep that I really need”.

ejercicios.frase: What she did next ___ phone her lawyer.
respuestas: was
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the wh-cleft used to highlight an action: What + subject + did + be + infinitive. The clue is “What she did next”, which is already the complete first part; what is missing is the verb be that links it to the focus. As “did” is in the past and the first part is singular, it is “was”. After it comes the bare infinitive “phone”, which would also allow “to phone”.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: The wh-cleft links the two parts with be: What she did was…
ejercicios.traduccion: Lo que hizo a continuación fue llamar a su abogado.

por_opcion.was: Correct: be in the past and in the singular joins the two parts of the wh-cleft.
por_opcion.did: Incorrect: “did” already appears in the first part; the link between the two parts is always be.
por_opcion.has: Incorrect: “has” does not work as a link and it does not agree with the past “did” either.
por_opcion.were: Incorrect: the clause “What she did” counts as singular, so be is “was”.

glosario.definicion_l: a professional person authorized to practice law; conducts lawsuits or gives legal advice

ejercicios.frase: It was only after the meeting ___ I understood the problem.
respuestas: that
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the it-cleft when an adverbial (of time, place or manner) is highlighted: the second part is introduced with “that”. The clue is the highlighted element, “only after the meeting”, which is a time expression; the card's typical mistake is using “when” in these cases. That is why “It was only after the meeting that I understood the problem”. “Only” strengthens the contrast: not before.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: The it-cleft uses that after a highlighted adverbial.
ejercicios.traduccion: Solo después de la reunión entendí el problema.

por_opcion.when: Incorrect according to the standard: in an it-cleft that highlights a time, “that” is used. You sometimes hear “when” in speech, but it is the mistake the card points out.
por_opcion.that: Correct: the it-cleft uses “that” after a highlighted adverbial.
por_opcion.which: Incorrect: “which” refers to an antecedent noun (a thing), not to a highlighted time expression.
por_opcion.then: Incorrect: “then” is an adverb (at that time, next), not a linking word; it cannot join the two parts.

ejercicios.frase: ___ was in Lisbon that they first met.
respuestas: It
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the card's it-cleft, which always needs the subject “it” before be. The clue is “___ was in Lisbon that…”: a subject is missing, and English, unlike Spanish, does not allow verbs without an explicit subject. That is why “It was in Lisbon that they first met”. It is the card's first typical mistake (“Was Peter who called you”).
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: The it-cleft needs the subject it.
ejercicios.traduccion: Fue en Lisboa donde se conocieron.

errores_previstos.respuesta: This
errores_previstos.explicacion: The it-cleft is always formed with “it”; “this” does not do that job.

errores_previstos.respuesta: There
errores_previstos.explicacion: “There was” introduces the existence of something; the subject of the it-cleft is “it”.

errores_previstos.respuesta: He
errores_previstos.explicacion: The subject of the construction is not a person but the empty “it” of the it-cleft.

ejercicios.frase: All ___ want is to be left in peace.
respuestas: I
we
they
you
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the card's variant “All I want is…” (the only thing I want is…), a type of wh-cleft with “all” instead of “what”. The clue is “All ___ want is”: the subject of “want” is missing, and it must be a personal pronoun. “I”, “we”, “they” and “you” are all correct, because they all agree with “want” without -s. “He” and “she” are not, as they would require “wants”.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: All + subject + verb + is: “the only thing I want is…”.
ejercicios.traduccion: Lo único que quiero es que me dejen en paz.

errores_previstos.respuesta: what
errores_previstos.explicacion: “All what” is a calque of Spanish “todo lo que”; in English you say “All I want” without “what”.

errores_previstos.respuesta: she
errores_previstos.explicacion: With “she” the verb would have to be “wants”; with “want” only I, we, you or they are correct.

errores_previstos.respuesta: me
errores_previstos.explicacion: You need the subject pronoun “I”, not the object pronoun “me”.

glosario.significado: que lo dejen a uno en paz

ejercicios.frase: The reason ___ I left was that I felt undervalued.
respuestas: why
that
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the card's variant “The reason why… is that…”, which highlights the cause. The clue is “The reason ___ I left”: after “reason” a relative clause is introduced with “why” or “that”, and both are accepted; it could also be left out. Note that the second part uses “that”, not “because”: “was that I felt undervalued”.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: The reason why/that… is/was that… highlights the cause.
ejercicios.traduccion: La razón por la que me fui fue que me sentía infravalorado.

errores_previstos.respuesta: because
errores_previstos.explicacion: “Because” does not introduce the relative clause after “reason”; you use “why” or “that”.

errores_previstos.respuesta: for which
errores_previstos.explicacion: “The reason for which” exists in very formal style, but the exercise asks for a single word: “why” or “that”.

errores_previstos.respuesta: what
errores_previstos.explicacion: “What” cannot go after an antecedent such as “reason”.

glosario.definicion_l: assign too low a value to · esteem lightly

ejercicios.enunciado: Highlight the word “Anna”, starting with “It was”.
respuestas: It was Anna who solved the puzzle.
It was Anna that solved the puzzle.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the it-cleft: It was + focus + who/that + rest of the sentence. The clue is the instruction, which asks you to highlight “Anna”, the subject of the original sentence and a person. That is why “It was Anna who solved the puzzle”, or with “that”, which is also accepted. Be is in the past to go with “solved”, and the rest of the sentence does not change.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: It was + focus + who/that + rest of the sentence.
ejercicios.traduccion: Fue Anna quien resolvió el rompecabezas.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Was Anna who solved the puzzle.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The compulsory subject “It” is missing.

errores_previstos.respuesta: It was Anna which solved the puzzle.
errores_previstos.explicacion: “Which” is used for things; for a person you use “who” or “that”.

errores_previstos.respuesta: It was Anna who she solved the puzzle.
errores_previstos.explicacion: After “who” the subject is not repeated: “who solved”.

glosario.definicion_l: a particularly baffling problem that is said to have a correct solution · a game that tests your ingenuity

respuestas: What I don't understand is his attitude.
What I do not understand is his attitude.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the wh-cleft: What + subject + verb + is + focus. The clue is the instruction, which asks you to start with “What”, and the object of the original sentence, “his attitude”, which moves to the end as the highlighted element. The “what” part keeps the negative: “What I don't understand”, and then “is his attitude”. The uncontracted form “do not” is also accepted.
ejercicios.traduccion: Lo que no entiendo es su actitud.

errores_previstos.respuesta: What I don't understand it is his attitude.
errores_previstos.explicacion: “It” is not needed: “what” already takes the place of the object of “understand”.

errores_previstos.respuesta: What I don't understand his attitude.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The verb “is” that joins the two parts of the wh-cleft is missing.

errores_previstos.respuesta: What don't I understand is his attitude.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The first part is not a question: the auxiliary and the subject are not inverted.

respuestas: What he did was sell his car.
What he did was to sell his car.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the wh-cleft used to highlight an action, which the card forms with do: What + subject + did + was + infinitive. The clue is the instruction, which gives the beginning “What he did”, and the original verb “sold”. The action moves to the end in the infinitive, “sell”, with or without “to”, and be is in the past and singular: “was”. That is why “What he did was sell his car”.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: To highlight the action: What + subject + did + was + infinitive (with or without to).
ejercicios.traduccion: Lo que hizo fue vender su coche.

errores_previstos.respuesta: What he did was sold his car.
errores_previstos.explicacion: After “was” the action goes in the infinitive (“sell” or “to sell”), not in the past.

errores_previstos.respuesta: What he did was selling his car.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The card's rule requires the infinitive, with or without to; the -ing form is not the standard structure here.

errores_previstos.respuesta: What he did is sell his car.
errores_previstos.explicacion: If the first part is in the past (“did”), be is also in the past: “was”.

ejercicios.frase: Is the noise that bothers me, not the heat.
respuestas: It is the noise that bothers me, not the heat.
It's the noise that bothers me, not the heat.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the card's rule: the it-cleft always needs the subject “it”. The clue is the beginning “Is the noise…”, copied from Spanish “es el ruido lo que…”, where there is no explicit subject. You just need to add “It”: “It is the noise that bothers me, not the heat”, or contracted “It's”. The final contrast with “not the heat” is a typical use of this construction.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: The compulsory subject it is missing.
ejercicios.traduccion: Es el ruido lo que me molesta, no el calor.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Is the noise that bothers me, not the heat.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: the compulsory subject “it” is missing.

errores_previstos.respuesta: It is the noise what bothers me, not the heat.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The second part of the it-cleft is introduced with “that”, not “what”.

errores_previstos.respuesta: This is the noise that bothers me, not the heat.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The construction is formed with “it”, not “this”.

ejercicios.frase: What I like most about her are her honesty.
respuestas: What I like most about her is her honesty.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the agreement rule of the wh-cleft: the verb be agrees with what is highlighted. The clue is “her honesty”, a singular (and uncountable) noun, so the verb must be “is”, not “are”. The correct sentence is “What I like most about her is her honesty”. The plural “are” would only be possible with a plural focus, such as “her eyes”.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: The focus is singular (her honesty), so the verb is is.
ejercicios.traduccion: Lo que más me gusta de ella es su sinceridad.

errores_previstos.respuesta: What I like most about her are her honesty.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: the focus “her honesty” is singular and requires “is”.

errores_previstos.respuesta: What I like most about her it is her honesty.
errores_previstos.explicacion: “It” is not needed: the wh-cleft has no other subject before be.

errores_previstos.respuesta: What I like more about her is her honesty.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Besides not correcting the mistake, it changes “most” to “more”; for “the thing I like most” you use the superlative “most”.

glosario.definicion_l: the quality of being honest · southeastern European plant cultivated for its fragrant purplish flowers and round flat papery silver-white seedpods that are used for indoor decoration

respuestas: It was my sister who told me
Was it my sister who told me
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the it-cleft: It was + focus + who + rest. The clue is the capital letter of “It”, which marks the beginning, and “who”, which introduces the second part. The focus is “my sister”, a person, and the rest is “told me”. The question “Was it my sister who told me”, with “was” and “it” inverted, is also accepted.
ejercicios.traduccion: Fue mi hermana quien me lo dijo.

errores_previstos.respuesta: It was who my sister told me
errores_previstos.explicacion: The highlighted element goes between “It was” and “who”: “It was my sister who told me”.

errores_previstos.respuesta: My sister was it who told me
errores_previstos.explicacion: The it-cleft starts with “It was”; the focus comes after.

respuestas: What worries me is the cost
The cost is what worries me
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the wh-cleft: What + verb + object + is + focus. Here “what” is the subject of “worries”, so no other subject is needed: “What worries me”. Then comes “is” and the focus, “the cost”. The inverted version “The cost is what worries me”, which puts the focus at the beginning, is also accepted.
ejercicios.traduccion: Lo que me preocupa es el coste.

errores_previstos.respuesta: What me worries is the cost
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the order of Spanish “lo que me preocupa”; in English the object “me” goes after the verb.

errores_previstos.respuesta: What is the cost worries me
errores_previstos.explicacion: The verb “is” joins the two parts and goes between “What worries me” and “the cost”.

descripcion_larga_es: Cleft sentences split a sentence in two to put the focus on one element: It was Maria who found the keys (es: “fue María quien…”), What I need is a holiday (es: “lo que necesito es…”). Since English cannot move the stress and word order as freely as Spanish, it uses them to contrast and highlight, especially when presenting and arguing.

contexto.que_es: They are constructions that divide a simple sentence in two to highlight one part. The it-cleft follows the pattern It + be + highlighted element + that/who + rest (It was Tom who broke the window). The wh-cleft or pseudo-cleft follows What + subject + verb + be + highlighted element (What I want is some peace). There are variants such as All I want is…, The reason why… is that…
contexto.por_que_importa: They allow you to contrast and correct (“it was Tom, not Ana”) and to organise information so that what matters comes at the end or in a prominent position. In an oral presentation or an essay they give clarity and a more elaborate tone, typical of C1 level. Badly built (without it, with when instead of that, with a plural verb) they give away a calque from Spanish.
contexto.cuando_se_usa: When you want to correct a misunderstanding, highlight who, when or where something happened, present a problem or a need (What worries me is…) or announce an action (What we did was…). Spanish achieves the same by moving words (“a María la vi ayer”) or with “fue… quien”; Spanish speakers often leave out the subject it (“Was Peter who…”) or use when/where instead of that.
